paper_metadata.title: Classical optimization with imaginary time block encoding on quantum computers: The MaxCut problem

summary: The paper proposes an imaginary-time block-encoding (ITE-BE) algorithm and a hybrid QAOA+ITE-BE method for MaxCut, simulated on unweighted 3‑regular graphs with N=6–12 nodes using up to 10^5 shots per instance. Both methods converge toward optimal solutions as imaginary time τ approaches ~2, with approximation ratios approaching 1 while post‑selection success probability decays exponentially. The hybrid approach improves post-selection success rate by roughly an order of magnitude compared with pure ITE‑BE for N=12.

experiments.description: Pure ITE-BE imaginary-time block-encoding method for MaxCut on randomly generated unweighted 3-regular graphs, evaluated by simulation across graph sizes N=6,8,10,12 and imaginary time τ∈[0,2].

algorithm.variant: Imaginary-time evolution block encoding (ITE-BE) for MaxCut
algorithm.convergence_criteria: τ varied until approximation ratio and optimal-solution probability saturate near 1

hyperparameters.first_layer_circuit: deterministic correction circuit for |+⟩⊗N initial state

problem_formulation.encoding_details: MaxCut encoded as diagonal Ising Hamiltonian HC = -Σ_{<j,k>} wjk/2 (I - ZjZk); one qubit per vertex plus one reusable ancilla qubit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize MaxCut cost C(s)=1/2 Σ_{<j,k>} wjk(1-sjsk) via ground state of HC
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on ancilla qubit; mid-circuit measurement/reset and shot termination on ancilla failure

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute approximation ratio, optimal-solution probability, and post-selection success rate from successful executions
